- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) or shows recent reversal, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for next 5 days.
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising prices) but sentiment turns negative, reduce forecast slope by 30–50% for next 5 days.
- If model forecast mean is > 10% above recent 7-day average, apply downward correction proportional to sentiment negativity (e.g., -1% per -0.1 sentiment).
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3+ days of decline after peak), model often misses it; adjust forecast to align with 7-day moving average if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history includes 2+ consecutive negative values, model tends to underestimate; add 3–5% bias to forecast for next 5 days.
- When model forecast is > 10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes or price stabilizes.
